No man’s Sky
overall
this game is not worth selling price, it is boring and extremely casual. I would not recommend paying more than 30AUD for this because there is a lot of better games you could get rather than this up priced boring game. there’s so many bugs that make the game frustrating and unpleasant, if you’re looking for story go somewhere else, if you’re looking for survival go somewhere else, if you’re looking for a fun exploration game, this is barely it. after four years this game is still as lack Laster as day 1 when I played it, if you want something to waste 30 odd hours on and then uninstall this is that but it’s certainly not any master piece and it isn’t that fun, 


-Story 2/5
I paid little attention to the story as it quickly became clear that none of my decisions mattered. All the text throughout the story felt slow and forgetful, so for majority of the game I did not bother to read any of it. None of the characters you met are interesting and same goes for the casual NPC you find floating around. My main issue with the story is how little it matters when it comes to what I say in dialogue. For example, in Fallout NV what you say will change the fate of the game or mission, or how much you may have to spend or how difficult it will be. In no man’s sky nothing matters. I could say anything, and it would all be the same so why does it give me an option? I could see this being fixed by adding more choice to the story but instead a lot of the missions are "find a hollo terminus" so I can briefly speak to someone and move on. 
-Missions 1/5
the missions feel extremely linear and are very repetitive they are often gone to point A read this then go to point B read this, then next mission. Or it follows the structure of get this, craft this, go here read, this. With no mans sky’s "30 hours of story" it is awfully lack lustre and I have no care for it. 
-Gameplay 2/5
No man’s sky has a lot of cool feature, but it doesn’t do any well. For example, trying to get minerals, the idea is to go around mine and collect. But why would I do that when I can just buy it? and it is often cheap and more convenient. Or why mine when I can get so much from looting a freighter, which brings me onto my next point. The dogfights. Once again a cool concept, there are a lot of weapons to choose from in your ship, but I soon realized how little I needed them. You can raid a whole fleet with a base ship and make millions, and at the most you get one or two sentinel ships coming after you which pose no threat whatsoever. Similarly, same thing goes with combat on a planet, however there is more variety in enemies (a total of 3) they sever close to no purpose. run a little distance away and they will leave you alone and they never were much threat even with a base blaster.
Factions! We all love factions as they bring a new aspect to the game. There are three main functions in No man’s sky, and there is an honour system with them, which is quite a good idea. Do contracts for a system get more rewards for future contracts. Sounds good? it is but having a negative honour with any faction changes nothing at all. In my playthrough I am an enemy of every faction, but I have no repercussion from either, making the honour system feel worthless. Maybe if the player had a negative honour with one faction maybe another faction would like you more? or maybe they faction that I was enemy with would not sell to me would make for more interesting gameplay and giving me more of a reason to raid fleets and mine for minerals
PLANETS! this was a huge selling point for no man’s sky when it came out and it still is. But after your first couple warps every planet starts to feel the same. My first planet was an extremely cold planet and two systems away I found basically the same planet. But that is not to say there are some cool planets because there are, but they are rare, and you will often come across bland planets with the same kinds of plants over and over.
Base building, its honestly kind of worthless. I did find my self-building bases and experimenting, but I rarely used it and I saw no reason to make a large one. everything I could do in a base I could do on a freighter. but fighters are expensive which leads to the next part
It is so god damn easy to make money, you can have all the money you could ever need within an hour or too because of the mass amounts of exploits in the game and these are well documented, 
Farming, farming in no mans sky is very basic. Plant a plant at the base, it grows, and then harvest. But this like many features’ serves no purpose, you can go the whole game and not have to plant anything ever. 
 

Petit comments:
The story is so unclear on what mission it wants you to do and it constantly changes, often it will tell you do to one mission why you have another activated and it often doesn’t even show you a marker on what you have to do. The game is also unclear on what it was not to be, is it survival? is its open world exploration? is it role play? I do not know frankly its boring. 
I have so many more comments about this game, but it is too much

Overall
This game is not worth selling price, it is boring and extremely casual. I would not recommend paying more than 30AUD for this because there is a lot of better games you could get rather than this up priced boring game. there’s so many bugs that make the game frustrating and unpleasant, if you’re looking for story go somewhere else, if you’re looking for survival go somewhere else, if you’re looking for a fun exploration game, this is barely it. after four years this game is still as lack Luster as day 1 when I played it, if you want something to waste 30 odd hours on and then uninstall this is that but it’s certainly not any master piece and it isn’t that fun,

Honestly, this game is gold. 

Ever since a couple days ago, I've decided to try it and it's all I've played recently. The main exploration factor has had me hooked - there is sooo much to see. There's no loading as you fly in or out of a world, and it is possible to fly to another star system, the only reason nobody has is because it'd be a really long fly. This tells me alone that this universe is possibly bigger than any other game. The ads for every game in existence say they have endless, huge universes but this may very well be the only game that truly does have an endless universe. 

But what's really appealing to me is the endless creature possibilities each planet has. Yes, I've seen multiple small birds with bat heads and once or twice I've even seen an almost exact copy of something I saw from other planets, but It makes sense that certain star systems have similar creatures. Different star systems generally have different life forms. And finding them and putting them on my catalog is fun in itself. But then different planets have some of the weirdest shit, too. And not creatures. Each planet has general foliage; trees, grass, small harmful plants. But you can find weird shapes in each world, and sometimes you just have to take a screenshot.

Something I find to also be cool is how easy it is to find a new ship. It's also a unique process of going into a space station and waiting for someone to fly in with a star ship you like instead of going to someone and buying one, which a lot of games do. And there's some really cool models to find. I'm sure I haven't seen all of them yet. 

Overall, the game has come a long way. I didn't bother when it first came out because I had heard it was really bad, but it's not anymore. I haven't played survival mode yet, but I surely will. What's interesting is the idea that each new game will be almost completely different. You'll have new creatures, new enemies to fight off, different views, and hell, even different materials depending on which planet you start on. Instead of your first playthrough being the only time you're excited to see what there is, every new game is that. 

I'd suggest it to anyone who loves life forms and pure exploration. You do need a bit of patience if you travel planet to planet in search of life forms like I do, because there's a certain number on each planet and it may take a while for you to find each one. Some are common, some are rare - and these for the most part are the ones you'll need to have patience for. Interestingly enough, sometimes your never able to find one that're supposed to be common, and if you look for long enough and you still can't find it just go to the next planet. But let me warn you; your gonna find some weird shit. Really, really weird shit.

No Man's Sky is a game of disparity, both within and without. On the surface lies a relaxed exploration experience where you explore the vastness of an endless universe, though you realistically wouldn't need to ever leave the galaxy you find yourself in. But it's what lies beneath that's so intriguing. Environmental storytelling has been used to varying effect in games and I'm happy to say that No Man's Sky does it right in that the small scraps you're given piecemeal through the experience invoke a desire to press forward and learn more. There's a lot of argument that No Man's Sky is "as big as an ocean and as deep as a swimming pool" usually making reference to once you've seen one planet of a specific type (there are a handful; Temperate, Hot, Cold, Toxic, irradiated, and Anomaly) then you've effectively seen every planet of that type. And there's certainly a good argument to be made. But I postulate a counter argument; the depth is not in exploring the myriad of planets available but uncovering all the little story bits that those planets house. What are the Sentinels? Why do they jealously guard certain planets? Why are their remnants so often found on the "anomaly" planets that show up from time to time? What is the Atlas? A benevolent god crying in pain for it's creation is seemingly being torn asunder? A sinister force hellbent on controlling the Travelers (that's you, the player!) and forcing them into a never ending cycle of life and rebirth, mindlessly gathering materials to make it to an arbitrary end only to start again? And then there's the three sentient races that dominate the universe and the secrets they keep. And it all boils down to one conclusion: in a very Lovecraftian cosmic horror-y way, something is horribly wrong with this universe. And I love every second of it. It's this context that gives the tedious grind meaning as you eek out your existence in this place you've found yourself with no real understanding of how or why. So land on those planets and go exploring. Find lost Ancient structures and secret manufacturing facilities and learn.

From a gameplay perspective, No Man's Sky has all the necessary trappings. You pilot a starship around the cosmos. This starship can be exchanged for different kinds of starships or just a better one if you like the kind of ship you have. I personally prefer Fighters and take the opportunity to get into space fights as much as I can. There are land and sea vehicles as well for when you land on planets which can make you combing them for resources and places easier to do. You can get technology to slot into your suit, Multi-tool, and vehicles to make the things they do better or add new functionality. Eventually you can be the owner of a massive Freighter which is not only capable of storing multiple starships and extra resources, but you can build a mobile orbital base and amass a fleet of frigates that can go out and return with goodies. If I sound less excited about all of this than the storytelling content above it's because all of this is perfectly serviceable gameplay but that's about it. It's not earth shattering. But it can be enjoyable, much in the way that you can enjoy Minecraft and just zone out collecting resources to build a base or whatever it is you're trying to do. Again, it's the context of the storytelling element above that gives meaning to the experience. Shooting at trees, rocks, and mining deposits with lasers over and over again doesn't sound fun in and of itself, but if while you're doing that your ExoCraft picks up a signal from some kind of facility that you journey to to learn one of the sentient races is doing some kind of weird experimentation on Sentinels, little moments like that make it all worthwhile. For me at least.

No Man's Sky is a weird game, that much is certain. And for some people it'll never be for them no matter what the Devs give it. I don't think there should ever be an expectation for anything high intensity. Massive chaotic space battles and fighting through sprawling alien metropolises fly in the face of the intended experience, which is a chill niche exploration game. But if the idea of flying around in a little ship gathering little tidbits of information without ever being given definitive answers in an incomprehensibly large universe and maybe building a base and seeing how filthy rich you can become, then this is definitely for you.

[h2]A little intro to this game[/h2]
this game may be the perfect exemple how a game dev team can redeem themselves!?! If you don't know the story behind this game and how it can back from hell, you should go watch the internet historian video about no man's sky "engoodening". At his launch back in 2016, this game was barren, and missed a lot of features hyped generated through it's development! I personnaly had a blast looking at his demise, it was a indy team, dumping so many feature idea through interviews and trailer, that the world hyped itself to the point that the game was bound to be the best game ever made! Reality is often disapointing, with so many missing feature, like multiplayer. The game review hit rock bottom! 
But instead of abandonning development and moving on to another title, the team broke it apart and rebuilt it to make a very enjoyable game to say the least! To stay with the multiplayer exemple, this week, they added cross platform multiplayer. After, adding multiplayer, base building, vehicules, cargos ships, exosuit... They still plan to continue the development to add new content.  
They did what most game should do in the case of a massive failure, get back to work and redeem themselves! Imagine if EA did that for anthem, we could have the best 3rd personne shooter/looter!

[h2]graphics and art[/h2]
-the graphics are amazin! For a 2016 title, they don't look dated at all.
-the art looks a little cartonney, this might be bad for some, i personnally love it as it is! Since most of the content is procedurally generated, i must have missed some of them during my 40hours playthrough, most of which i saw were well made!
-the biome diversity, is a bit low in my opinion, which brings something lessen the "it's magical" feeling after going through the same biome multiple times!

[h2]Sound design[/h2]
-the sound in this game is a bit lacking in my opinion, the robot voice that tells you when thing are lacking in your suit is somewhat nerving in my opinion. Other than that, the space ship, player, etc... are somewhat nice.
-The music are cool and fit the "adventure" theme. Since, most of the G@m3rz now, play with their own music background, this might not be relevant anymore, put whatever suit you the most, though, i would recommand some peacefulll music to go along the way, it might give you a stardew valley feeling!

[h2]Gameplay[/h2]
-[spoiler]i won't spoil any part of the main plot! no worries![/spoiler]
-This game is mostly a sandbox game, this falls into "make your own fun" categories! You start with mostly nothing, a broken ship, a laser pistol that basically does nothing! your ultimate goal is to cross the galaxy and go into the central blackhole. Along the way, multiple plot line, can be followed,(or not, it's up to you!). There are many ressources, in form of atoms and molecules, you can buy or sell them, to get better ship and equipement, but most of them are consumed by your equipment, for instance, your life module, will need oxygen to keep you safe, your laser will need carbone. It's up to you to find the most efficient way to get the balance and turn some into profit! Along the ressources, there are 3 types of money, the credits, aka, the cold hard cash, that you will need to get ships and buy ressources, nanites, which will be used to buy upgrade for equipement and ships, and silver, which have cosmetic purposes only!
-DON'T WATCH YOUTUBE VIDEOS! especially, tips and tricks types, or credits farm! credits farming and how to be efficient with its spending, is a huge part of the game in my opinion, if you spoil yourself with youtube video, you WILL ruin your fun! 
-Base building is pretty fun, if you are the "builder" type in minecraft, you will love the possibilities, otherwise, if you are like me, a creature with nothing like creativity, there are prefabs which allow you to make quick and "efficient" base, like "big square room", "circular room".
-The spaceship is somewhat hard, to drive at first, but you will get used to it fairly quickly, the spacefight are a bit clunky du to this but after you get some equipement, they gets a lot more enjoyable! The only "disapointing" part is that the shield can be recharged instantly by pressing 3keys, it kinda feels like they knew that the combat system was clunky and made it so you can't die if you pack enough ressources. 
-The other vehicule in general didn't really strike me as needed. it's a bit sad but they come somewhat late in the game, and you will probable have enough upgrade for your spaceship and exosuit, that it'll be more efficient to go by foot or take your spaceship. the exonef control are really disturbing, you can't walk directly somewhere, the mecha will walk in circle, which is a shame, because it's one of the most usefull vehicule for it's combat power!
-The mining and excavation are fun, it gives a minecraft vibes, with better tool, discovering new ressources, adding upgrade to your mining laser feels fresh each time!
-The combat are pretty basic in this game. This is most lacking aspect of the game. This and the lack of enemies. As seen in the trailers, you will mostly fight, wildlife and sentinels, some robot like police man, that shoot before it talks. With a GTA like research bar, with the last one bringing the big boy bipeds tanks to kill you. This will be the only enemy that will give you a bit of challenge, since one of the weapon, the grenade launcher, is way OverPowered and will butcher anything it comes across(including you so beware bad bounce). The mecha, is a beast for fighting with rocket, guns, etc.. that will destroy these bipeds tanks. Even in fps mode, the combat are slow and a bit boring. 

[h2]Other[/h2] 
-This game optimization is AMAZING! i also tested it on a whooping GeForce 750m 2gb and it ran pretty well by lowering the resolution, with the Ui scaling option, the game was enjoyable with such small config! LOWSPEC GAME UNITE, this game is for you!
-The game is still lacking a good endgame! Within 40hours, i have accumulated few hundred millions and can produces more with farms, but the game really miss a money dump, some way to used billions and billions other than buying expensive ships!
-Another point i think they should add, is a easy way to convert credits into nanites, you can balance the number nanite, credits conversion rate, but you can already do that in game but it is so painfull. 
-I encounter very few bugs in my playthrough, and only one game breaking one which makes this caution : don't build "small square room" and put a teleporter inside, this will get you stuck, and unable to destroy said room to free yourself!

I strongly recommand this game for everybody regarless of their specs. If you love the sandbox genre, go for it! the story isn't that bad except the part where [spoiler]SYKE, i told you that i won't spoil anything[/spoiler]! O;

No Man's Sky is to my view an incredible game. It changed a lot to become how it is at the moment. This game allows you to play on 256  different galaxies for an amount of 18,446,744,073,709,551,616 planets (you will never explore them all). There is not any specific goal except the main quests which are already quite long, but the thing is that you are free to explore everything. You can upgrade your ships and equipments with a class system (C,B,A,S), and you can obviously make some optimization to collect essential ressources, to get some money or to craft stuff, etc... There is an economic system which allows you to send your own ships through solar systems to get some rare ressources or money (it just depends on what kind of expedition it is). The game owns something called the "Anomaly station", it allows you and your friend to meet people or even to start missions with strangers. For a few days now, the developers added the cross platform, so you can now play with Steam, PS4 and XBox players in the same group.

Do I need a good config to play it ?
This game is pretty good optimized in terms of performance, but you'll need a GPU which has at least 8GB of RAM to run the game with the highest textures resolution.

Is it a long game or not ?
To be honest it's kind of an infinite game, it all depends on what you rather do, but if you like exploratin and optimization, it can quickly turn into a quite infinite game.

Is there a lot of players ?
There are around 7000 players, and there are 256 galaxies but everyone spawn in the galaxy called Euclid, so your best chance to meet someone will be there, because with 18,446,744,073,709,551,616 planets, I doubt you'll meet someone by chance. By the way, the Anomaly station allows you to meet people as well.

Do you need a good conenction ?
Not really, you can even play this game with 2000ms, it doesn't matter as long as you're alone on your solar system. 

Is it a buggy game ?
Yeah, there are many bugs, and a lot to exploit, but using them makes the game boring, so you better not use them or you'll regret your purchase. 

Are the developers active ?
Yes they are. They are often adding new features, and fixing many things, just be patient and they'll improve the game even more, but it is already great.

How is the gameplay ?
It's pretty difficult to learn, but easy to master when you understand it.

Is it worth it ?
The price is quite expensive, but I do not regret my purchase at all.

At it's core, this game is all about grinding. You grind for resources. You grind for money. You grind for words so that you can understand the people around you. The game is only about filling up a series of meters that lead to nothing.

While you are supposed to explore, there is nothing really to explore. Due to the random nature of the game, most planets look the same. The only difference is the type of hazard you have to deal with.

I wish I could give two reviews for this game Single Player Experience and Multiplayer Experience.

The single Player game is great and really does a good job immersing you into the vastness of space and just how insignificant you are.

The multiplayer game is barely that.  You can group up and travel around together fine.  Doing anything that really feels "multiplayer" is just too buggy to ever work.

Here is my main issues with Multiplayer:
-  Bases don't load for everyone, they either can't see my base or they see my base but their instanced world still has all the terrain that I removed to build said base.
-  Missions aren't designed for multiple people (except the anomaly based ones which I'll get to).  The missions are created for single player play.  Crashed ship?  One person get's it!
-  Anomaly MP is a good try but is still broken.  Full party doesn't always load into mission.  Often 2/3 out of 4 people are in the same instance while one or two are thrown by themselves on the same mission but not linked.
-  The random events that DO NOTHING are mind boggling.  Giant crashed freighter in space? No story, no distress signal, no ominous music, JUST SHOOT CARGO POD AND GET MINERAL OK THANKS HURDUR.  Preserved colony organism floating through space?  Small flavor text and guess what? SHOOT IT!  

If you like solo space exploration with a decent building and vehicle system give it a try.  If you want to space fly with your friends who cant stop watching Firefly again and again, wait for Starbase.

Reviews.131847:
When No Man's Sky was first announced I was pretty excited. When it came out I was surprised about all the really bad reviews. But seems people were rightfully disappointed.

4 years later, and after hearing that Sean and his team did not "run with the money" and did not leave the game behind, but instead worked obviously very hard to get things right and keep promises they made for the original release, I got this game now...

...and I seriously love it! The universe is huuuuuuge, but thank god not empty. I'm only around 40 hours in and still have not seen anything close to what it offers. There's tons to do: exploration (planets, ships, stations, artefacts), trading, building up a fleet of capital ships, more exploration, crafting, mining, even more exploration, space battles...

Compared to what I've seen the game looks changed quite a bit, and I personally do like it. It's stylized, but not so much over the top like it had been, immersion is really well handled. Sound is glorious (one of the rare games I do not feel the urge to shut the music down).

"Dangerous Elitists" might think the ship controls and realism is lacking, and it is... NMS controls more arcady, and that is fine by me. I do not have to learn hundreds of keybinding to get my ship going, and in this case I am glad about it. NMS is more like a melting pot of many many game genres... and in my opinion it shines in pretty much all of them.

Tons of respect to Sean and the team for staying on the project, for learning from past mistakes (the PR dilemma Sean called upon himself by jumping hisa own hypetrain and almost getting torn to pieces by it). In my eyes everyone earned a second chance, and Hello Games absolutely managed to turn this trainwreck of a game around and change it into something that is fun deluxe! Thank you for this!

Now stop reading my review already and gooooo explore!

I consider myself lucky to have skipped the whole hype train / hate train surrounding the game's launch. If you consider buying it now and are interested in the whole drama I recommend you watch the Internet Historian's take on No Man's Sky crazy redemption: https://youtu.be/O5BJVO3PDeQ  
I bought it shortly after NEXT's release and Oh boy, did this game deliver.

No Man's Sky is a crafting game akin to Minecraft, but with far sexier graphics, a quite touching Asimovian backstory,  and space travel. THIS  DOES MEAN: crafting games aren't for everyone, they essentially challenge the player's patience and ability to learn from the game's massive environments and "alchemy" mechanics. The game is a slow burn and is the most rewarding when the player takes his time. Just don't get in expecting a Mass Effect Trilogy generator -this games does not exist-. If you're into the game's premise, NMS will provide an almost zen experience, with all it's flashy colors, improbable critters and post-rock music.

The game can played anyway you'd like, whether you want to:
- be a basebuilder / architect
- an explorer
- a survivalist
- an anthropologist 
- a space drifter
- a linguist
... and so on. It really is up to the player to find out what kind of space traveller he wants to be.  Not to mention the whole online quest thing HG implemented with the Beyond Update. Also from what I've experienced, the game has one of the friendliest community around.

I could go on and on, but this is just a short opinion piece. All in all No Man's Sky is an adorable game.

Awesome, game. I have to recommend it because it is really good. BUT, there is one huuuuuge problem with it. 

There is absolutely no sense of achievement, There is a truly HUGE amount of content, the problem is, you have it all within a matter of hours. 

The first hour of the game you fix your ship. Take off in to space, super cool. You warp to another system, and boom, a huge fleet of awesome looking ships, they're under attack, you kill the 2-3 super weak fighters attacking, the captain of the giant freighter invites you on board, "Woooo time to get paid." So you dock and go to speak to him, he says, "Hi stranger, thanks for shooting those tiny ships that we could have clearly taken ourselves with our 50 massive frigates.....Here take my ship for free"

Wow, now I have a massive ship capable of storing everything including all my small ships....Ummmm, now what? I literally just had a tiny fighter I started the game with an hour ago, now I have this?

Then, you find the anomaly, you spend a couple hours on a planet digging up data to turn in for stuff, now I have every single exo craft, every single building part, weapon and upgrades for everything, I build my cool massive base, it took 15 minutes, now I think, "let's explore a bit," only, what's the point? I already have everything, I've played for a day and I have literally everything. Now I am bored and have absolutely no incentive to keep playing.

Such a shame, because this game is fantastic, so much stuff, but when you give someone everything, instantly, the game literally commits suicide in front of you, an amazing game that I couldn't wait to play, and it just killed itself right in front of me within days :-(

There needs to be a level system, there needs to be progression, there needs to be something to aim for, because giving you everything instantly, completely destroys the game. 

I have 75 hours in game as of now, but that is game open time, and half of it is actually in the pause menu where game time isn't added to your save. (not for any game related reason, just I tend to leave games open when I go off to do other things) My actual save file is about 40 hours play time, and I have everything, I want to keep playing, but the few things I have left to get, which is really just the submarine and living ship, which as cool as they are, would extend my play another day at most, then I am back to having nothing to play for.

Such a shame, it is a truly amazing game, that shoots itself in the head almost instantly.

First of all I need to admit that I have joined really late, therefore a lot of stories of how bad it was and how good it is are not part of this review. Nevertheless I see a lot of progress already. I witnessed the living ship and minotaur updates so far and some bugfixes.

This game is absurdly large besides countless star systems, there are:
— at least some sort of a story.
— flexible base construction on ground, underwater, and aboard the freighter ships.
— speaking of freighters you can hire a fleet that will go out on an expedition and bring you money and valuables. Don't forget to maintain the ships and craft enough fuel for them.
— agriculture, domestication and riding animals.
— somewhat real economics, allowing you to earn on low buying and high selling prices.
— easy but plentiful crafting and cooking.
— multiplayer tasks.
— almost seamless starship traveling from takeoff off one planet to landing onto another, loading screens only when traveling from system to system.
— black holes that will warp you somewhere across the galaxy.
— portals that will warp you exactly where you need to be if you know the hexadecimal address.
— planets with anomalies, suddenly all flora, fauna and minerals are hexagons or bones or bubbles.
— dogfights with pirates right in the middle of an asteroid belt.
— cars, bikes, submarines, hovercrafts and other vehicles.
— up to six specialised starships in your freighters' garage.
— digging, scanning, shooting and mining with your multitool and sentinel drones that think you shouldn't.
— backpack, serving as an inventory, portable refiner, jetpack, hazmat suit in case of bad weather and whatnot.
— countless types of really bad weather, including toxic rains, radiation, frost, heat, desert planets with both depending on day or night, the most pleasant of all, piping hot rains.
— earning a good name among three races and three guilds.

There are still some things that i don't like, including:
— freigher bases that are gone with the wind, when you buy a new freighter, because you've earned this.
— basically leaving everything behind when you move to the next galaxy.
— the more of the same in the next galaxies, despite we are unlikely to entirely explore even the first one.
— little replay value, since you've played through the story, there's little sense to go on. You can still search for particular anomalous planets, take missions from nexus or mission agents, buy vanity items, polish your base, buy better ships and tools, but sooner or later it feels useless even as a sandbox.
— fps dependant mouse sensitivity, a real pain in the neck when you try to fight pirates or sentinels.
— not really wide FoV even in the widest settings.
— spaceflights and on foot exploration are optimised for first person perspective, but exocrafts are almost impossible to use any way except in third person view.

All things combined I still think this is a game that's worth its' price and should be played. There are a lot of things to do and a lot of things to see.

Reviews.134751:
[h1]Only buy this when you can get it for 20€ or less, it's not worth it even on a -50% sale (~28€) and definitely not full price[/h1]

[h1]Review for the mentally challenged:[/h1]
lyin' devs put bug in mah soup 5/10

[h1]TL;DR review for people with no time:[/h1]
Good when you haven't spent too much money acquiring it. Otherwise it's a buggy mess with updates being centered around adding more gimmicks than fixing bugs.

[h1]Review with more than 100 words:[/h1]
I bought this game on GameBillet for about 19€ and for that price it is an indie game definitely worth checking out for the amount of content and quality it provides. There are people that ask [i]"What's this game about? What's the point of it all?"[/i] and after playing it myself I can say [i]No Man's Sky[/i] is less about the goal and more about the journey. It's more akin to a sandbox game like Minecraft where you make up your own stories and own goals. Want to go to the center of the galaxy as fast as possible? Want to stay on a planet for 10 hours and simply build bases, craft and go on treasure hunts? Go solo or co-op with others? It's all possible. If you are a fan of sandbox games I'd say go for it. The main "plot" quests are simply there to teach you the game, get you some new crafting technologies and get you from point A to point B.

However the reason I say it's worth picking up for 20€ or less is because that's as much as I was willing to play for a massive yet (very) buggy and controversial indie game. If I had bought this game for more this review would have probably ended up being negative, especially since the game gets pretty repetitive and boring after 30 to 35 hours. I wonder what it was that made the developers think they could sell this for 55€ full prize.

Of all the bugs I have encountered some of them even seem to exist since the NEXT update that came out almost 2 years ago without any fixes since then whatsoever. The developers seem to be more interested in adding new gimmicks with every update than to fix simple, game breaking bugs that even modders could fix in five minutes, but I expected nothing less from the people who released this game in 2016 in a very miserable state after lying through their teeth about all the features this game would supposedly have but did not.

[h1]PROS:[/h1]
- It was really fun for the first 35 hours I played (after that I simply went achievement hunting to keep me invested)
- Open sandbox game akin to Minecraft, Terraria etc.
- Massive improvement compared to the 2016 original release version
- Mod support

[h1]CONS:[/h1]
- Lots of bugs (see below)
- Planets and the game in general become pretty repetitive after a while
- Performance drops, either happening at random  (save re-load required) or whole planets not being optimized (who's brilliant idea was it to make a planet full of reflecting church windows?)
- Overly long "Hold to confirm" action commands on everything you want to do (fixable with mods)
- Learning alien languages is an extreme grind as each language seems to consist of over 750 words and you have to learn them each word for word (fixable with mods)
- Each update breaks mods
- Major updates seem to be focused on adding more and more gimmicks than to fix longstanding bugs

[h1]BUGS:[/h1]
[b]Selection of bugs I have encountered, ranging from minor to major ones. Don't expect these to be fixed any time soon (if ever).[/b]

- Planet surface textures (and textures in general) take forever to load and can even downgrade in quality right in front of your eyes no matter your graphic settings, making the game look like puke (fixable with mods) > https://i.imgur.com/nlH7Z4M.jpg
- Rebinding keys does not rebind all commands in the game (e.g. rebinding the scanner from "C" to "Q" doesn't rebind the ship's scanner as well, it's still activated with "C" despite the game telling you to press "Q")
- First-person camera seems to lock up every now and then after leaving a menu/NPC
- First-person weapon getting stuck in some weird position below your view, making it impossible to see if you have it equipped or not (game restart needed to fix)
- Sound effects randomly not playing (footsteps, ship engines etc.)
- Entering an Exocraft, driving 50 meters away from your base and coming back makes all the base doors disappear (save re-load needed to fix and being able to enter your base again) > https://i.imgur.com/fsGw5Z2.mp4
- Getting stuck on small 1 inch ledges on the floor so you have to jetpack over them (even in popular and often visited areas like in the upgrade area of the Space Anomaly (why is this even a thing?)) > https://i.imgur.com/5h4AEl3.mp4
- While tunneling with the multi-tool the game randomly decides to put you back onto the surface every now and then (broken failsafe) > https://i.imgur.com/Iss8VX4.mp4
- Communication holograms offscreen > https://i.imgur.com/AqdJtwe.jpg
- AI ships fly through solid ground > https://i.imgur.com/fAd1MyO.mp4
- AI bases have invisible outside walls > https://i.imgur.com/N250mv9.jpg
- You can peek through cave walls while underground, seeing the unloaded outside world and planet surface > https://i.imgur.com/fUANGch.jpg

[h1]OVERALL:[/h1]
☐ 5/5 (Great)
☐ 4/5 (Good)
[u]☒ 3/5 (Okay)[/u]
☐ 2/5 (Bad)
☐ 1/5 (Terrible)

[h1]ESSENTIAL MODS:[/h1]

Fine LOD (fix texture load times): https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1316
Fast Actions (less time wasted on "Hold to Confirm"): https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1081
Learn Words Faster (decrease language learning grind): https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1139

Reviews.136357:
[h1]🟩 Pros[/h1]
+ World & System exploration
+ Base building and manipulating the ground
+ Exceptional when playing with friends
+ Major content is released in patches and not DLC's
+ Very active modding community @ Nexus

[h1]🟥 Cons[/h1]
- Various bugs here and there
- Normal difficulty (Survival is the intended experience!)

[h1]🍒 Additional personal opinion[/h1]
Considering the great flop at launch they have really improved themselves overtime making this game truly enjoyable both single & multiplayer. There's still a few bugs left, but nothing really gamebreaking (that I have encountered thus far) 

Exploring the different systems is quite interesting as you encounter the weirdest and wondrous things, however even with their engine and tweaking it gets quite monotonous. It's highly recommended to venture to Nexus and fetch a world generation mod that's based on the vanilla world (to prevent clipping through ground when teleporting to others bases through the hub)

(The best thing about this game is that you can mod the hell out of the game, but you can still play with a vanilla-friend/stranger as they are all client side, while you may be able to cheat/cheese through the game this way I highly suggest you don't because you will kill the longevity of the game, and the only one suffering is you!)

Exploring the world with a friend is recommended as it gets less lonely, however there's some silly limitations/rules in multiplayer that may screw with you or your friends in terms of desyncs, but nothing gamebreaking, only slightly annoying.

If you love exploring without overly complicated shipcontrols, want to build yourself a base and venture into space to either fight pirates, mine ore or do trade runs then this game is for you.

Just remember to start the game on Survival, as it is way more fun than "Normal" (which should be relabeled into "Toddler-mode" where almost everything you need to complete the entire game is located in very close vicinity of your starting planet. There's also no real danger on any planet. 

Survival is hard in the very beginning, but gets progressively more enjoyable after you've set up your first base.

This game was cooler on the release day. I am not trolling. Hear me out.

I always have been a suсker for exploration-driven games. So when I heard about NMS in 2014 or so, I was [i]ecstatic[/i]. A game that promises infinitely many procedurally generated worlds, plants, and animals? Set in a setting that would allow me to explore space as well?! Sign me up! I preordered this game both for me and for one of my friends.

When this game came out, it lagged. It was terribly grindy, even worse than now. It was, at times, ugly. [u]But it was about EXPLORATION[/u]. NMS in 2020 is yet another survival game. It is [i]beautiful[/i], but it came at the cost of [i]variety[/i]. Nowadays, it's the same snow biome, the same desert biome, the same animals everywhere. There is some uniqueness here and there, but it is shoved to the background in favor of such mechanics as base-building, vehicle driving, and other stuff I couldn't care less about.

It has finally become clear to me that this direction of development is not going to change.

If you want yet another grindy-shooty-basebuildery survival game, sure, go ahead, buy it. It's not bad in that regard, pretty great even. However, my disappointment is immeasurable, and my [strike]day[/strike] decade is ruined.

Reviews.185492:
7/2/20. So I am back in the game and actually quite enjoying it.  It took a long time but NMS is finally becoming what was imagined so many years ago.  If only more developers had this passion.  The best part is that all these additions to the game are free!  No expensive DLC. Many of the old things that were frustrating are gone.  Most of the terrible grind is gone.  Inventory space is no longer microscopic as the stack sizes have been increased and there are numerous ways to increase the various inventory slots. Basic resources are much easier to come by. Exocraft make getting around a planet so much nicer than running everywhere.  If you find a cool starship you can upgrade it and keep it.  There are also now many tutorial based missions that help explain a lot of the mechanics and where to find many of the various resources in the game but the wiki is still required if you really want to get into it.  There still are some monotonous areas if you really want to get into base building and upgrading everything in terms of resource gathering but that comes with any game like this.  

Planets are more varied now but they could still be better.  One frost planet still looks like the next, and the next, and the next. Exotic Biome planets are neat but fairly useless and almost a little to common.  

There are still some bugs, nothing game breaking.  

Overall there is plenty of content here now to keep you busy without just trying to reach the center of the galaxy.  If you like survival, exploration, space, and building,  NMS finally is able to fulfill those needs.  Oh, and I finally did find a t-rex, and a sentinal walker.   

Old Next Review:

So I have not touched this game since its first release.  With NEXT now out I thought I would give it another shot.  All I can say is THE GRIND IS REAL.  Add a few more things, make it look nicer and multiply the original grind times 10X and you have NEXT. I want to like this game but the new super slow progress just ruins it.  

I started a new game as there are so many new mechanics out there you really have to start a new game to understand them.  I have spent about 10 hours on a new game and progress is slow.  Only a couple of slots added to my exosuit, can't afford any new multitools.  I found my first crashed ship and after three hours of just focusing on it I still don't have it completely fixed. The amount of resources it takes and the extremely slow gather rate it takes forever.  At this rate it will take 1000+  hours just to get a fully upgraded ship.  It really is about survival as I spend near around 50% of my time just trying mine to refuel my multitool and exosuit so I can mine.  I will jump into my old save since I don't have 1000 freaking hours and see but I still really cant recommend this game even though I really want to.

OLD Original REVIEW:

Insane: Definition; Continuing to repeat the same tasks with no noticeable results or outcome. Synonym; No Mans Sky.    

If there is anything I can say about NMS is that it simulates the emptiness of space and the monotonous repetiton of survival very well.  A huge ground breaking game with not a whole lot in it. NMS is best played casually at your own pace a little bit at a time.  If you like story, structure and action, NMS is not for you.   If you are looking for a space sim, this is not it.  If you like setting your own goals and just exploring, then NMS will fit you well.  Out of the 60+ hours I have spent in NMS, maybe 10 were fun.

Surviving at first is fun.  Fixing your ship up, upgrading your exosuit and multi-tool, finding bigger ships is all fun at first.  The first time you get off your planet and start discovering new planets, new systems.  But after a while every planet starts to look the same, hey that one creature has two more legs than the last one.  

There are a few really nice planets. A lot of barren dead ones.  Again, realistic space. I think in 200+ I visited during my trip there were 2 that I enjoyed and a handfull of memorable creatures.  The rest is a blur.  Getting to the center of the galaxy quickly becomes a boring chore.  Refuel, Repair, Warp, Repeat.  Do this for 24+ hours and you will get there.  Finding that one resource you need to fix your broken hyperdrive from the last black hole will give you a nice frustration headache.    

NMS is stable now in its latest build.  Before the patches this game was an absolute nightmare of instability.  

Get this game on sale if you want it.  It may be huge, and eat a lot of your time, but the fun factor is just not there.  I wish there was a neutral recommendation but I have to say for $60, no.

PS. I never did find a sentinal walker.

There is no faction to 'join', or fight for
There is no fleet battle to see or fight in
There is no living economy, or even a trade convoy in all of space
There is no sand planet, and there are no sand worms

It quickly becomes clear how few unique-looking ANIMALS there are
It quickly becomes clear how few unique-looking SHIPS there are
It quickly becomes clear how few unique-looking PLANTS/RESOURCES there are

Space combat is unsatisfying and inferior to just about any space game
Ground combat is incredibly unsatisfying and vastly inferior to most 1st person games
A clunky, slow, and inconvenient UI that gets in the way of gameplay instead of enhancing it

Reviews.202578:
Let me give you some history about my reviews on this game.  When NMS came out, I gave it a scathing review and in my opinion it was well earned.  The game almost seemed to be intentionally marketed with features that they knew it would not have.  The most profound was multiplayer.

That made news headlines in the gaming communities. While Sean, the producer of No Man's Sky was touting on Twitter that two players had just "met up in game", what he failed to say was they could not see each other.  To me, this seemed like a cover-up.  Instead of an apology or an aknolwedgement that they couldn't see each other, he still tried to perpetuate the lie, that the game was multiplayer with very distinct and carefully crafted language in his tweet.

I bought the game for myself and about 8 different friends because I thought it would be multiplayer.   So the disappointment after the release was a very large factor in my review.  

There were a few more factors that I'll lightly touch on:

1) The RNG for animals made no sense
2) There was no end-game content, no real reason to keep progressing
3) Nothing was bigger or better than a hauler and it was easy to obtain
4) There was no multiplayer

Today, every gripe I had does not exist today.  Instead of like most producers, Sean lived up to his promises and added multiplayer to the game 2 years later.  When I heard about this, I changed my review after a few hours of gameplay to recommended and said exactly this -- nothing was true in my review any more.

It is true, the RNG made more sense. There was now what I would call end-game content, with ship classes that range from C to S.  There were now very rare ships in the game you could get, capitol ships and frigates that will assist you in combat.  And, there was full-scale multiplayer that had enough thought put into it that it allowed for cooperative building.

Unfortunately, the honeymoon of the NEXT update quickly wore off for me, and many other players.  But it's not a lack of features -- but mostly bugs.   But I know, that's not fair.  You don't give a negative review to a game because of a few bugs.  I usually do not unless those bugs are persistent, gamebreaking, or, as in this case, the company claims to fix them, yet does not.

After a few months, and another update to this review (2 now), the bugs seem to be mostly worked out and the game is once again playable. 

PROS:

1) Fully featured Space Game
2) Multiplayer
3) Freedom to roam and do as you wish
4) Base building that rivals most other building games
5) Decent game-play progression
6) Great visuals with some exceptions (see below)

CONS:

1) The story is lacking
2) This is not a space simulator - nothing about flight or orbital mechanics are close to realistic.
3) Post-processing needs an overhaul - clouds are still buggy
4) While this is a survival game, essential mechanics are noticeably missing, such as food and water consumption to stay alive although there is oxygen consumption

Overall the gameplay is very decent while the game does lack any story line (what story line there is, I won't spoil it by going into detail about this).  Therefor, I've changed my review once again to RECOMMENDED.

Initial Thoughts: Since I have been following the development of this game for a considerable time I purchased it based on what I had read and seen pre-release. Pre-release reviews are very hard to gauge considering the title has been in development for five years and many things with regard to game play and styling changed throughout development, however as I like the game style and the genre (I play elite and I enjoy Sci-fi) I was going to buy it anyway regardless.

Play Style: Just like in Elite Dangerous there is grind, it's unavoidable if you want to craft, buy a better ship or purchase items through the market. The crafting system is straightforward and eases you into more complex recipes as you progress through the game. You have to hunt for elements and manage inventory slots in order to create the more complicated stuff like warp fuel (this can also be purchased from traders). You gain credits from selling discovered items, places or materials on the market or by selling to traders either on the planets or on space stations. The markets are very simple and cannot be compared to the likes of elite or eve, however they are functional. 

The flight model is basic with simplified controls but fits in with the styling of the game. Don't expect a DCS is space this was not what the game was designed to be like. Combat on the surface and in space is pretty basic. I could find no way of locking a particular target (unless I missed this control somewhere) however I could stand my ground easily against a few targets at once. Weapons like everything else in the game can be upgraded and added to through the crafting system.

Closing thoughts: There seems to be a large number of negative reviews about this game, many are as a result of the game either crashing, poor frame rates or just not starting at all. Some reviews have been made with 30 mins of game-play, how a proper view of a game can be made in so little time I just cant understand?? Many of the issues seem to be linked to AMD chips. As I run on an Intel i7 clocked to 4.7Mhz, 32gb of ram and use a GTX 980Ti I have experienced no problems with regard to frame rates or crashes. There was some stuttering to begin with but this disappeared after the day one patch.

Overall I like this game, If you like crafting, Trading, exploring and the Sci-Fi genre then you will enjoy this game go buy it! It's still OK.
